ExperienceHero.title: Professional Experience
ExperienceHero.description: A timeline of shipping production web applications, migrating legacy architectures to microfrontends and building scalable design systems since {careerStartYear}.

EvolutionBlueprint.text: From monolith enterprise systems at Glintt and HUUB to microfrontends at PriceHubble and schema-driven components at Teya, taking on more technical ownership each time.

bulletPoints: On my own initiative, identified and made codebase improvements in an existing financial operations application, refactoring its structure while still delivering features quickly.
Contributed to migrating state management from legacy Redux and Recoil to Context API patterns, reducing complexity and bundle size.

Led the migration of components from Chakra UI to an internal design system based on Material UI, including a dynamic component engine that rendered complex workflows from JSON configurations and data schemas.
Used AI in day-to-day work to explore solutions, map tech debt and speed up delivery, with every change reviewed by me before it shipped.

Maintained and extended a large multi-tenant platform supporting production web and hybrid mobile applications, adapting interfaces and localised business logic for high-volume international restaurant brands.
Implemented a unified Stripe payment integration, dynamically configuring the payment form's appearance, verification flow and client branding via tenant schema rules.
Owned feature implementation, integration tests and the handoff to QA teams, fixing regression defects and running production releases with no downtime.
Worked with another engineer to plan, design and deliver the first phase of splitting a large Angular monolith into microfrontends, separating the business domains.
Set up separate repositories and CI/CD deployment pipelines, using single-spa to coordinate routes, so independent product teams could deploy on their own.
Built a redesigned user onboarding wizard in React and Next.js, iterating closely with a product designer to improve the UX and step-completion metrics.

Joined as the company's first frontend developer, setting the engineering conventions and building its first application on my own to streamline second-hand luxury handbag acquisition and authentication.
Designed and published version 1.0 of the company's internal component library, standardising interaction design, visual tokens and reusable building blocks across its separate business tools.

pedrobarbosa-pt.name: pedrobarbosa.pt
pedrobarbosa-pt.tagline: The website you're on, built and run like a product
pedrobarbosa-pt.summary: My personal website, where I show my experience and projects. I treat it like a product at work: a prioritised backlog, small focused commits, and checks that must pass before anything goes live. I used AI to build it faster and reviewed every change myself.
pedrobarbosa-pt.details: Every push runs formatting and lint checks, type checks, tests and a production build, and a failing check blocks the deploy. Every page is sent with security headers that only let it load the site's own files, and browser tests try script injection, framing and redirect attacks against it. The code is public, so you can see how I work, not just read about it.

takeaways.title: Quality gates
takeaways.text: Formatting, lint, type checks, tests and a build run on every push, and nothing deploys unless they pass.

takeaways.title: Tests that survive refactors
takeaways.text: Tests check behaviour and edge cases through what visitors see, so they only change when the behaviour does.

takeaways.title: Structure with rules
takeaways.text: Folder and import rules are enforced by lint, so each file's scope is clear from its path.

detailCards.title: Quality & Delivery
detailCards.description: Component and page tests on every push, with deployments that wait for them to pass, plus browser and accessibility tests in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, run locally and against the live site.

growth-tracker.name: Growth Tracker
growth-tracker.tagline: An investment tracker that shows your real average price
growth-tracker.summary: A product I took from idea to launch. Users logged their assets, buys and sells, and Growth Tracker calculated the average price they could actually trust when deciding to sell.
growth-tracker.details: Buy 3 units at 500 and sell 1 at 700, and a typical broker app shows an average of 400, even though the remaining units still cost 500. Growth Tracker kept that number accurate, so users could aim for a profit on every unit they sold.

takeaways.title: Product ownership
takeaways.text: Defined the business rules and requirements myself, starting from a problem I had.

takeaways.title: End-to-end delivery
takeaways.text: Built every layer, from the database to the interface, and took it to launch.

takeaways.title: Making value obvious
takeaways.text: Learned that a strong feature isn't enough if users can't see its value. I had plans to address it, but the money ran out first.

detailCards.title: Frontend Implementation
detailCards.description: Implemented a designer's visual design, including asset management, the transactions table and a chart tracking how the real average price evolved with each transaction.

detailCards.title: Backend & Core Logic
detailCards.description: Built the backend and data model, plus the complex algorithm behind the real average price, covering scenarios like sales made below it.
